newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian opposition leader seeks caretaker govt.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian opposition leader seeks caretaker govt.

text.p: A caretaker government should lead Cambodia to the next general elections if relations between co-premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen continue to deteriorate, the country's opposition leader said on Monday.

Sam Rainsy, president of the officially unrecognised Khmer Nation Party, flew home after several weeks raising funds overseas and told reporters the country was headed for disintegration unless political and diplomatic measures were taken immediately.

He said Ranariddh and Hun Sen, whose royalist FUNCINPEC party and the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run elections in 1993, should work and make decisions together again so that government can function normally.

"All the political forces in Cambodia must be convinced to work together so that the national assembly (parliament) can meet, because without the national assembly meeting no law can be passed...especially the electoral law," he added.
The coalition and parliament have been effectively paralysed since Hun Sen in mid-April gave his support to a challenge to Ranariddh's leadership of FUNCINPEC from royalist dissidents.
Ties between the partners were battered when a deadly grenade attack on March 30 ripped through an opposition demonstration led by Sam Rainsy, who formed an alliance with FUNCINPEC earlier this year.
The two premiers, in a bid to allay fears of a coup bid or violent confrontation, have since pledged to desist from military force and agreed to end a war of words on television and radio.

Sam Rainsy said that if Ranariddh and Hun Sen were unable to resurrect their working relationship, "I have suggested that this government be changed into a caretaker government until the next elections." Polls are due by the end of 1998.

He said the caretaker government would ensure a minimum of order, security and public services and would not make commitments on behalf of the nation but must concentrate all efforts on preparation of free and fair elections. Polls are due by the end of 1998.
"I think it is up to FUNCINPEC and the CPP and to the major donor countries to elaborate and refine this idea," Sam Rainsy said.

Sam Rainsy has blamed Hun Sen for the March 30 attack, which killed up to 19 people and wounded scores more, and on Monday he said he believed the co-premier would make another attempt on his life. Hun Sen has denied the charges.
